data.description:
URLQuery report d35771c5-15fc-4591-af6b-6864ba0450ba records a concrete data-return mechanism on May 14, 2026 (UTC). A custom encoded browser page retrieved a UNCTAD statistical archive through CodeTabs and exposed its contents through outgoing request URLs that the scanner retained. This allows verification of returned data even when a separate response-body download is unavailable.

The wrapper loaded at 00:35:20.142. At 00:35:20.699, the program's CodeTabs request received HTTP 200 with a recorded 176,441-byte archive. Between 00:35:21.135 and 00:35:21.305, the program emitted 79 GET requests carrying numbered pieces totaling 235,256 Base64 characters. Offline ordering and decoding of those recorded URL pieces reconstructed the entire 176,441-byte archive and matched its recorded SHA-256. The archive contains a single CSV with 15,716 data rows and 19 columns. The hash check was performed by the investigation; the captured program did not itself calculate or verify the hash.

The 79 requests are output chunks from one upstream archive retrieval, not 79 separate dataset downloads, people or runs. The important result is verified content recoverable from scanner request logs. An HTTP status alone would be weaker evidence; here the reconstructed bytes and hash provide the content check. Splitting data across URLs is consistent with keeping individual outputs manageable, but the record does not establish that a particular browser/server/scanner size limit forced the design.

This is an instance of using a browser-based scanning service for research retrieval and scanner-visible output. It does not demonstrate malicious exfiltration, authentication bypass, unauthorized access, or compromise of the statistical source. There is no authenticated actor/model/provider attribution and no proof that a different agent later read these output chunks. UNCTAD is part of the United Nations system rather than a national or state/local government, so the form's government classification is marked Unsure. The preserved report is already reviewed; the submission does not claim a substantial newly untapped source. Historical code was decoded and reconstructed offline rather than executed during review.
data.summary: A May 14, 2026 URLQuery program fetched a UNCTAD archive and emitted 79 numbered output requests. Their recorded URLs reconstruct the complete 176,441-byte archive, including a 15,716-row CSV, demonstrating scanner logs as a data-return channel.
